reasons: Most Deploy links lead to a not-found page.
The search only checks name, tagline, and description, not capabilities or outcomes.
No tests are visible in this file.

terms.meaning: values a page remembers while it runs, such as which filter is selected
a rule that hides items that do not match a chosen value
a unique label React uses to track each item in a repeated list
a web address that leads to a page, such as the tools address
a rule that an item must pass every condition at the same time to be shown

used_by: The Next.js router, for the /tools web address (not imported by another file in this packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and industry list
sections.what: Loads React state, animation, links, icons, the custom tech icons, and the shared industry list that the filters use.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The industry list is imported, which suggests it is shared with other parts of the app.
sections.watch_out: Industry ids used on each tool must match the ids in the shared industry list, or the filters will miss those tools.

sections.name: Tool
sections.title: Shape of a tool entry
sections.what: Describes the fields each tool must have: id, name, tagline, description, category, icon, pilot length, outcomes, key capabilities, industries, and whether it can be customized.
sections.why: Gives every tool the same structure so the page can display all of them in the same way.
sections.watch_out: The icon field is loosely typed, so a wrong icon will only show up when the page runs, not when the code is written.

sections.name: tools, categories (part 1)
sections.title: Tool data, first three tools
sections.what: Defines ARCHITECT, ORACLE, and PULSE, each with description, outcomes, capabilities, industries, and customization flag.
sections.why: Acts as the catalog the page filters and displays. No database or fetch is visible in this file.
sections.watch_out: Each tool id here should match the detail page address it links to, or the Deploy link will fail.

sections.name: tools, categories (part 2)
sections.title: Tool data, next two tools
sections.what: Defines SENTINEL, which is marked as not customizable, and PRISM, which answers business questions about data in plain language.
sections.why: Continues the catalog so the page has all the tools to show.
sections.watch_out: SENTINEL is marked not customizable, so it disappears when the Customizable Only switch is on.

sections.name: tools, categories (part 3)
sections.title: Last tool and category names
sections.what: Defines APEX, then the list of category names used for the category filter buttons: All, Strategy, Finance, Research, Operations, and Analytics.
sections.why: Keeps the category names in one place, since the filter buttons are drawn from this list.
sections.watch_out: A tool whose category is not in this list cannot be reached by any category button, apart from All.

sections.name: ToolsPage (part 1)
sections.title: Filter state and matching rules
sections.what: Remembers the selected category, industry, search text, and customizable-only switch, then keeps only the tools that pass all four checks. Search ignores capital letters and checks name, tagline, and description.
sections.why: Each filter narrows the list further, and the list updates the moment a filter changes.
sections.watch_out: All four checks must pass together, so a combination of filters can hide every tool.

sections.name: ToolsPage (part 2)
sections.title: Count badge, headline, search box, filter header
sections.what: Shows a pill with the number of matching tools, the two-line headline and intro text, and the search box. It then opens the sticky filter bar with the Filter by Industry label and the Customizable Only toggle.
sections.why: Lets a visitor see how many tools match and search from the top of the page.
sections.watch_out: There is no custom tool promo box in this range. Do not describe one here.

sections.name: ToolsPage (part 3)
sections.title: Industry and category filter bars
sections.what: Draws the Filter by Industry row with an All Industries button and one button per industry, the Show All or Customizable Only toggle, and the category button row. The filter area sticks to the top while scrolling.
sections.why: Keeps the filters visible while the visitor scrolls through a long list of tools.
sections.watch_out: Industry buttons come from the shared list, so a new industry appears here automatically but will show no tools until tools are tagged with it.

sections.name: ToolsPage (part 4)
sections.title: Tool grid and no-match message
sections.what: Shows a no matches message when the filters remove everything. Otherwise shows a two-column grid of tool cards, each with its icon, name, a Custom badge when allowed, tagline, and category.
sections.why: Gives a clear message instead of a blank area when nothing matches.
sections.watch_out: Cards are identified by their tool id, so two tools with the same id would break the grid.

sections.name: ToolsPage (part 5)
sections.title: Industry tags, description, and capabilities
sections.what: Shows up to three industry tags, the tool description, and the first three key capabilities with check marks.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each card short while still giving a quick summary.
sections.watch_out: Each industry tag shows only the first word of the industry name, so two industries that start with the same word look identical.

sections.name: ToolsPage (part 6)
sections.title: Card footer, Deploy button, and closing banner
sections.what: Shows the pilot length and a Deploy button on each card that opens that tool's detail page. Then a closing banner invites visitors who are unsure which tool fits to launch the console.
sections.why: Deploy is the main action on each card. The closing banner gives a path for visitors who are not sure which tool to choose.
sections.watch_out: Deploy leads to a detail page, but only the AI Strategy Advisor has one, so most Deploy buttons will show a not-found page.

summary: Catalog page that lists the AI tools, lets visitors search and filter them by industry, category, or customizability, and links each card to its detail page.
purpose: Helps a visitor find a suitable tool for their sector or problem, and move on to its details or to the console.
why: Reason for the layout not stated in the code. The on-screen text says filters help find tools proven in a sector, which matches the design.
how: Keeps the tool list and category names in plain data. Stores four filter values: category, industry, search text, and customizable-only. Keeps only the tools that match all four. Then draws the header, the sticky filter bar, the grid of tool cards, and a closing section.
inputs: Clicks on filter buttons, typing in the search box, and the tool list and category list defined in this file, plus the industry list imported from another file.
outputs: A filtered grid of tool cards, a count of matching tools, and links to each tool's detail page and to the console.
risks: Most Deploy buttons lead to detail pages that do not exist, because only one tool has detail data. The tool data is duplicated from the detail page and can drift apart. The icon field is typed as any, so a wrong icon is not caught early. Filters depend on exact matching ids.
debug: If a filter shows no tools, check the tool's industries or category values against the industry list and the category list. If Deploy shows Tool not found, check the toolDetails list in the detail page file. If the count seems wrong, check the filter logic near the top of the page function.
